lines.en: Tom, do you have a minute? I would like to talk about something that is not easy to say.
lines.pt: Tom, você tem um minuto? Gostaria de falar sobre algo que não é fácil de dizer.

lines.en: Of course, Pam. You sound worried. Has something happened?
lines.pt: Claro, Pam. Você parece preocupada. Aconteceu alguma coisa?

lines.en: Yesterday the director told me that the Denver project would end next month.
lines.pt: Ontem o diretor me disse que o projeto de Denver terminaria no mês que vem.

lines.en: Oh no. Did he say why it was being stopped?
lines.pt: Ah, não. Ele disse por que estava sendo interrompido?

lines.en: He explained that the budget had been cut, and he asked me to tell the team gently.
lines.pt: Ele explicou que o orçamento tinha sido cortado, e me pediu para contar à equipe com delicadeza.

lines.en: I see. I was afraid something like this would happen. Did he say what would happen to us?
lines.pt: Entendo. Eu tinha medo de que algo assim acontecesse. Ele disse o que aconteceria conosco?

lines.en: He said that nobody would lose a job, but he warned me that some people might change teams.
lines.pt: Ele disse que ninguém perderia o emprego, mas me avisou que algumas pessoas poderiam mudar de equipe.

lines.en: That is a relief. I asked him last week whether we would get news, and he promised me an answer.
lines.pt: Que alívio. Perguntei a ele na semana passada se teríamos notícias, e ele me prometeu uma resposta.

lines.en: I told him that you had worked extremely hard and that the team deserved honest information.
lines.pt: Eu disse a ele que você tinha trabalhado muito e que a equipe merecia informações honestas.

lines.en: Thank you for being so kind. May I ask when the others will be told?
lines.pt: Obrigado por ser tão gentil. Posso perguntar quando os outros serão informados?

lines.en: This afternoon. I will let you know how they react, and you can help me answer their questions.
lines.pt: Esta tarde. Eu aviso como eles reagem, e você pode me ajudar a responder às perguntas.

words.ex: To say something gently is to be soft.
A budget is the money for a plan.
To deserve is to earn something.
Relief is a calm feeling after worry.
To react is to answer to something.
An honest person tells the truth.

teach.goal: Ponte português → inglês com palavras úteis.
solo: Peça uma frase pessoal com 2 das palavras.
group: Palavras: gently, budget, deserve, relief, react, honest.
Aluno diz em português um uso real, depois a palavra em inglês.
extra90: Cada aluno escolhe a palavra mais útil e explica por quê.

facts.big: He said that… would… · She asked whether… · told me that…
facts.label: Discurso indireto
facts.sub: Recue o tempo: will → would, has → had. Perguntas: if/whether + ordem direta. Told me that…; said that… Explained, warned, promised.

facts.label: will → would
facts.sub: No discurso indireto, o verbo recua um passo: will vira would, present vira past e present perfect vira past perfect. He said the project would end. Isso vale quando o verbo de relato está no passado.

facts.label: Whether / if
facts.sub: Para relatar perguntas, use ordem de afirmação e if ou whether: He asked whether we would get news. Sem do/did e sem ponto de interrogação. Compare Where is it? e He asked where it was.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: In reported speech, will often changes to would.
Present perfect often changes to past perfect.
In reported questions, we keep the question order.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: In reported speech, will often changes to would. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Present perfect often changes to past perfect. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
In reported questions, we keep the question order. → Falso (We use statement order.)

pages.title: Breaking the news gently · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cold morning in Denver, and snow covers the mountains in the distance. Pam has a meeting with the director early in the day. She has received bad news about the team’s project. Tom is her closest colleague, and he trusts her. Pam wants to choose her words carefully. She calls Tom into a small, quiet room.

“Tom, do you have a minute? I would like to talk about something that is not easy to say.” says Pam. “Of course, Pam. You sound worried. Has something happened?” says Tom. “Yesterday the director told me that the Denver project would end next month.” says Pam.
